next_state_election.name: Maine General Election
next_state_election.source_name: Maine Secretary of State — Upcoming Elections

glance_notes.text: Maine's November 3, 2026 General Election includes federal, state and county offices. Ranked-choice voting applies to federal offices in the general election when the statutory conditions for ranked-choice tabulation are met; state general-election offices such as Governor and the Legislature are decided by plurality.
glance_notes.source_name: Maine Secretary of State — Upcoming Elections

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: You may register to vote in Maine if you are a U.S. citizen and have established your fixed and principal home in the Maine municipality where you register. Maine allows preregistration beginning at age 16; to vote in a general election you must be 18 by Election Day, and a 17-year-old may vote in a primary if they will be 18 by the related general election. You can register online through Maine's Online Voter Registration Service, by mail, through certain state agencies, or in person with your municipal registrar or clerk — including on Election Day. First-time Maine registrants must provide information and documentation sufficient to verify identity and residence. Maine's official guidance lists government photo ID, certain non-photo government documents, official documents showing your name and address, and a student photo ID issued by a qualifying Maine school or institution among documentation a registrar may consider. If you register in person and cannot provide satisfactory proof of identity and residence, Maine law provides for your ballot to be treated as a challenged ballot rather than simply turning you away.
register.source_name: Maine Secretary of State — State of Maine Voter Guide
register.internal_note: Registration proof and identification at the polls are different rules. Maine SOS expressly says an already-registered voter does not need to show ID to receive a ballot.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Maine directs voters to their municipal clerk or registrar to confirm whether they are registered to vote. The Secretary of State maintains an official searchable directory with contact information for municipal clerks and registrars. Maine's Voter Information Lookup is useful for polling-place and ballot information, but the Secretary of State's clerk directory specifically says to contact your municipal clerk to check registration status.
check_registration.source_name: Maine Secretary of State — Find a Municipal Clerk or Registrar

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: Maine's current law sets different registration deadlines by method. Applications submitted by mail or by a third person must be received by the close of business on the 21st day before Election Day; online applications are due by 5:00 p.m. on the 21st day before Election Day. Registrations transmitted through the Bureau of Motor Vehicles or another designated source agency may be received through midnight on the 7th day before Election Day. In-person registration remains available through the close of the polls on Election Day, so Maine has same-day voter registration.
deadlines.glance_value: Online/mail: 21 days before; in person: through Election Day
deadlines.source_name: Maine Revised Statutes, Title 21-A §121-A — Deadline for registration
deadlines.internal_note: PL 2025, c. 397 created the current method-specific deadlines. Reverify after legislative updates.

polling_place.label: Find a Polling Place
polling_place.content: Use Maine's official Voter Information Lookup Service to find your voting place from your home address. The service also shows candidates and ballot information. Maine warns that municipalities may update voting-place locations until as late as 10 days before an election, so check again shortly before Election Day.
polling_place.source_name: State of Maine — Voter Information Lookup Service

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: If you are already registered, check in with the election officials at your voting place by stating your name and residence address; Maine law then provides for the election clerk to check your name on the incoming voting list and issue the ballot or ballots you are entitled to receive. Maine's Secretary of State explicitly states that an already-registered voter does not need to show ID to get a ballot. If you are not registered, you may register in person on Election Day; you will be asked for proof of identity and residence. If satisfactory proof is not available, Maine provides a challenged-ballot process rather than requiring the voter to leave without voting. If you are in line at 8:00 p.m., you are still entitled to register and vote.
election_day.source_name: Maine Secretary of State — Your Right to Vote in Maine

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: Polls generally close at 8:00 p.m. on Election Day. In municipalities with fewer than 100 people, polls may close earlier once every registered voter has voted (Title 21-A §626(2)). Opening times are set locally within limits established by state law: polls generally open no earlier than 6:00 a.m. and no later than 8:00 a.m.; municipalities with fewer than 500 residents may open as late as 10:00 a.m. Municipal officials set the actual opening time, and the election notice must state the opening and closing times. Voters present at the voting place at closing time must be given the opportunity to vote. Check your municipality's exact hours before Election Day.
polling_hours.glance_value: Local opening time; polls generally close at 8:00 p.m.
polling_hours.source_name: Maine Revised Statutes, Title 21-A §626 — Polling times

early_voting.label: Early Voting
early_voting.content: Maine distinguishes formal 'early voting' from the in-person absentee voting it currently offers. The Secretary of State says Maine currently allows in-person absentee voting rather than a separate Election-Day-style early-voting process. Any registered voter may vote absentee without giving a reason. In-person absentee ballots are available at the municipal clerk's office during the 30 days preceding an election, while the clerk's office is open (Title 21-A §753-B(8)). Absent a statutory special circumstance, the deadline to request an in-person absentee ballot is the third business day before Election Day — ordinarily the Thursday before a Tuesday election (Title 21-A §753-B(2)(D)).
early_voting.glance_value: No-excuse in-person absentee voting before Election Day
early_voting.source_name: Maine Secretary of State — Early Voting Reports
early_voting.internal_note: Maine SOS explicitly distinguishes 'early voting' from in-person absentee voting, unlike the NH inference issue.

absentee_mail.label: Absentee & Mail Voting
absentee_mail.content: Any registered Maine voter may vote by absentee ballot without giving a reason. You may request a ballot through the state's online absentee service when it is open, by contacting your municipal clerk, or by using the state's request form. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, Maine's online request service is active. Under the general rules, the statutory deadline to request an absentee ballot is the third business day before Election Day — ordinarily the Thursday before a Tuesday election — unless a statutory special circumstance applies (Title 21-A §753-B(2)(D)). You may also vote absentee in person at your municipal clerk's office during the 30 days preceding an election while the clerk's office is open (Title 21-A §753-B(8)), subject to the same third-business-day deadline. A completed absentee ballot must reach the municipal clerk before the polls close on Election Day (Title 21-A §755). Maine also offers online ballot tracking. Beginning December 31, 2025, Maine allows any voter other than a UOCAVA voter to apply for ongoing absentee-voter status, which can provide an absentee ballot automatically for elections for which the voter is eligible.
absentee_mail.glance_value: No excuse required; request deadline is the 3rd business day before Election Day
absentee_mail.source_name: Maine Secretary of State — Absentee Voting
absentee_mail.internal_note: The statute contains varying effective dates. The SOS page confirms the expanded ongoing absentee-voter status is in effect as of 12/31/2025.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: Maine has different identification rules for registration and for an already-registered voter checking in to vote. If you are already registered, the Maine Secretary of State states that you do not need to show ID to receive a ballot. When registering — including registering on Election Day — you must provide proof of identity and residence. Maine law lists several kinds of documentation a registrar may consider, including government-issued photo ID, certain non-photo government documents, official documents showing your name and address, qualifying Maine student photo ID, or verified identifying numbers. If a person registering in person cannot provide satisfactory proof, Maine law places the voter's name on the voting list and treats the ballot as challenged; the voter is not simply denied a ballot. Maine's challenged ballots are initially counted like regular ballots, with their validity examined later only if necessary under the statutory challenge process.
voter_id.glance_value: Already registered: no ID required to receive a ballot
voter_id.source_name: Maine Secretary of State — Your Right to Vote in Maine
voter_id.internal_note: Cross-checked against Title 21-A §§112-A, 121, 671, 673 and 696. Do not describe registration documentation as a general Election Day voter-ID requirement for already-registered voters.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: Maine provides an Accessible Voting System at every polling place. The state's system uses the ExpressVote ballot-marking device so voters with disabilities can mark a ballot privately and independently, with features that include accessible visual and audio interaction. Maine also offers an accessible electronic absentee ballot for voters with disabilities that prevent them from independently marking a paper ballot; eligible voters can request it through the online absentee-ballot system and use compatible assistive technology at home.
accessible_voting.source_name: Maine Secretary of State — Accessible Voting

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: Maine provides special registration and absentee-voting procedures for voters covered by the Uniformed and Overseas Citizens Absentee Voting Act (UOCAVA), including qualifying uniformed-service voters and U.S. citizens living overseas who were or would have been qualified to vote from a Maine residence before leaving the United States. UOCAVA voters may register online or use the Federal Post Card Application (FPCA), which can both register the voter and request absentee ballots. Maine's guidance says an FPCA request can cover elections within 18 months of submission. UOCAVA voters use the Secretary of State's military/overseas procedures rather than the ordinary municipal absentee-request timetable.
military_overseas.source_name: Maine Secretary of State — Uniformed Service and Overseas Voters

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: A college student may register and vote in the Maine municipality where they attend school if they have established a voting residence there — their fixed and principal home for voting purposes. Maine's Secretary of State says that residence may be a dorm, apartment, house or even a hotel, and paying out-of-state tuition does not by itself prevent a student from establishing a Maine voting residence. Students are subject to the same residence standard as other voters and may have only one voting residence. Registering to vote in Maine may create separate obligations to update information with other government agencies, but the Secretary of State states that completing those other updates is not a prerequisite to registering or receiving a ballot.
student_voting.source_name: Maine Secretary of State — Maine Voting Residence Fact Sheet

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: Use Maine's official Voter Information Lookup Service to see election information for your home address, including the candidates who will appear on your ballot and an official sample ballot when available. The same service provides your voting-place location and elected-official information.
sample_ballot.source_name: State of Maine — Voter Information Lookup Service

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: Maine Department of the Secretary of State, Bureau of Corporations, Elections and Commissions, Division of Elections — 184 State House Station, Augusta, ME 04333-0101; physical location: Burton Cross Building, 111 Sewall Street, 4th Floor, Augusta, ME 04330. Elections Division phone: (207) 624-7650; Bureau phone: (207) 624-7736; elections email: cec.elections@maine.gov. The Division of Elections is open Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. For local registration, absentee-ballot and polling questions, Maine also maintains a searchable directory of municipal clerks and registrars.
contact.source_name: Maine Secretary of State — About the Bureau of Corporations, Elections, and Commissions

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Maine Secretary of State — Elections & Voting provides the state's central election information; Upcoming Elections provides current statewide election materials and dates; the Voter Information Lookup Service provides polling-place, candidate and sample-ballot information by home address; the Find a Municipal Clerk or Registrar directory provides local election-office contact information; and Maine's online voter-registration and absentee-ballot services handle registration and absentee requests directly through official state systems.
official_resources.source_name: Maine Secretary of State — Elections & Voting
